subject: QR code
prompt: The QR code was invented in 1994 by a Japanese firm to keep track of what?
why: Masahiro Hara designed it at Denso Wave for labelling automobile components on the production line. Phones and menus came decades later.

subject: Nobel Prize
prompt: Five Nobel Prizes come from Alfred Nobel's will. Which sixth was added in 1968 by Sweden's central bank?
why: Nobel's will named physics, chemistry, physiology or medicine, literature and peace. The economics prize was endowed later by Sveriges Riksbank in his memory, which is why it is not strictly a Nobel.

subject: International Space Station
prompt: Besides NASA, Roscosmos, ESA and JAXA, the fifth partner agency running the space station belongs to which country?
why: The Canadian Space Agency is the fifth partner. China is not a partner at all -- it built its own station, Tiangong.

subject: Daylight saving time
prompt: What do the UK and the EU officially call the practice of putting the clocks forward?
why: It is 'summer time' in Britain and the EU and 'daylight time' in the US and Canada -- the same one-hour shift under two different names.

subject: HTTP 404
prompt: An HTTP 404 is proof that which part of the process actually worked?
why: 404 means the browser reached the server perfectly well and the server could not supply the resource. A server you cannot reach at all gives you a different error entirely.

subject: Coffee
prompt: Coffee beans are not beans at all. What are they?
why: They are the seeds of the coffee cherry, the fruit of the Coffea plant, separated and roasted before grinding.

subject: Blood type
prompt: Your blood type is set by antigens sitting on the surface of which cells?
why: Inherited proteins, carbohydrates and glycolipids on the red cell surface define the group. Some of the same antigens appear on other tissues too.

subject: Ivy League
prompt: The Ivy League is, formally and originally, what kind of organisation?
why: It is an NCAA Division I athletic conference of eight private universities. The academic prestige attached to the name later; the league itself is about sport.

subject: Order of the British Empire
prompt: The Order of the British Empire was created in 1917 by which monarch?
why: George V established it during the First World War to recognise service outside the battlefield, which is why it reaches so far beyond the military.

subject: Uranus
prompt: Which planet has recorded the coldest temperature in the Solar System, colder even than the planet beyond it?
why: Uranus has hit 49 K (about -224 C), lower than anywhere on Neptune despite Neptune being further from the Sun.

subject: Eurovision Song Contest
prompt: Eurovision was modelled on which country's national song festival, running since 1951?
why: The Sanremo Music Festival inspired the European Broadcasting Union to launch Eurovision in 1956.

subject: Dalai Lama
prompt: The title Dalai Lama was first conferred in 1578 by whom?
why: Altan Khan gave the title to Sonam Gyatso in thanks for his teachings, and it was applied backwards to the whole lineage.

subject: Pacific Ocean
prompt: The Pacific is the largest of Earth's oceanic divisions. What other superlative does it hold?
why: It is both the largest and the deepest ocean; the Mariana Trench lies within it.

subject: Amish
prompt: The Amish are an Anabaptist group tracing their origins to which two European regions?
why: Their Swiss and Alsatian roots explain the Pennsylvania German they still speak, and their close relation to the Old Order Mennonites.

subject: Yin and yang
prompt: In Chinese philosophy, yin and yang are opposite forces that are also what?
why: They interact, support and perpetuate each other -- neither can exist alone, and the whole is greater than either part.

subject: Ganesha
prompt: Ganesha's title Pratham Pujya marks him as the god worshipped when?
why: Hindus of many denominations invoke Ganesha at the start of a ritual, a journey or a new venture, regardless of which god the ceremony is actually for.
